title: Expected-time randomized recognition implies RP
statement: Let $L$ be a language of bit strings in the class of languages recognized by a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with a polynomial expected-time bound, where random choice bits select its transitions. On members, for every $\varepsilon>0$ some number of random bits gives probability at least $2/3-\varepsilon$ of halting with output true; on nonmembers, every halting run outputs false. Then $L$ has an efficient one-sided randomized verifier in the polynomial-time verifier model: it accepts members with probability at least $2/3$ and rejects nonmembers with certainty.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ belongs to the union, over exponents, of the stated expected-time randomized machine classes.
